title: Graph-Based Personalized Memory for LLM Agents: Representation, Evolution, Retrieval, and Evaluation
claim: The survey summarizes representative personalized-memory benchmarks and their evaluation metrics, organized into five metric groups.
explanation: The evaluation section lists benchmarks such as LoCoMo, LongMemEval, PersonaMem, and others, and groups reported metrics into answer quality, evidence retrieval, user-state modeling, memory evolution and structure, and efficiency. This provides a structured summary of evaluation practices.

blocks.text:
ActMemEval [62]
tests whether retrieved memory supports implicit con-
straint and counterfactual reasoning, while ATM-Bench [63]
adds multimodal, multi-source personal evidence. Struct-
MemEval [64] asks whether memory is organized correctly.
Across these benchmarks, reported metrics fall into five
groups:
•Answer quality:F1, exact match, multiple-choice accu-
racy, task success, and LLM-as-judge score.
•Evidence retrieval:Recall@k, NDCG@k, answer-turn
retrieval accuracy, evidence-location accuracy, and mul-
timodal evidence recall.
•User-state modeling:preference-category accuracy, pro-
file or persona consistency, and correctness or helpfulness
of personalized responses.
•Memory evolution and structure:update success, step
or chain accuracy under changing environments, forget-
ting/update outcomes, structure-requiring task accuracy,
and failure-attribution

Personalized graph memory remains a young but promising
research frontier. Its central challenge is not merely storing
user information in graph form but building a long-term,
trustworthy, and actionable model of an individual user, which
in turn motivates several future directions.
